What this means
AI answers are built on third-party automotive sources

Automotive specialist media, comparison platforms and marketplaces together account for 61.5% of all citations. Brand-owned content plays a minor role in how these answers are assembled.

Influence is concentrated enough to act on

The top 20 sources drive 48.5% of citations and the top 50 reach 69.3%. More usefully, the gap concentrates in a handful of page types on specific themes — label eligibility content, hybrid and 7-seater buyer guides — rather than spreading evenly across publishers.

OMODA & JAECOO can strengthen presence across the sources AI already uses

The official OMODA/JAECOO site receives 68 citations (0.83%) and the wider official-plus-dealer ecosystem 87 (1.06%), while competitor OEM sites collect 903. The gap is largest, however, in third-party environments — the specialist media, comparison platforms and marketplaces that carry most citations.

The immediate opportunity is off-site

The immediate opportunity identified by the Source Map is off-site: strengthen OMODA & JAECOO presence and contextual linking across the third-party sources AI already relies on, starting with the most cited publishers identified here.

Owned pages remain important as the destination of these links and will be assessed in more detail during the subsequent GEO Diagnosis.

What this Source Map is forIt identifies the external sources ChatGPT and Gemini already cite in this category, and where OMODA & JAECOO are present or missing within them. It is the evidence base behind the media and content proposals HAVAS Media will bring forward: which publishers to prioritise, which article formats to ask for, and where editorial coverage should link. It measures citation behaviour, not media performance.

What this tells usTwo clear patterns. First, the highest-cited editorial pieces are almost all recurring comparison and buyer-guide formats — "mejores SUV calidad-precio", "coches con etiqueta ECO", "SUV 7 plazas", warranty comparisons — not news pieces. Second, most of them currently show no OMODA or JAECOO presence. Inclusion in this type of evergreen guide is the concrete ask when contacting a publisher.

What this tells us

Interpretation
  • Specialist automotive media is the backbone. One in three citations comes from this group — it is the primary battleground.
  • Comparison and marketplace platforms act as gatekeepers. carwow.es, quecochemecompro.com, coches.net and autohero.com sit in the top six despite not being editorial media.
  • Institutional sources own the label questions. dgt.es and race.es dominate ECO and CERO answers, where brand content has limited leverage.
  • General editorial media is a smaller but reachable layer — relevant because it maps onto HAVAS editorial-group relationships.
Opportunities & activation
Where OMODA & JAECOO can strengthen external presence

The external sources to prioritise, what to ask each of them for, and how to use editorial and paid coverage to link into the right pages. Everything in one place.

Methodological disclaimerOverlap between influential AI sources and media or editorial partners creates an opportunity to reinforce the availability, consistency and authority of OMODA & JAECOO information across sources already used by AI systems. It does not mean media investment produces citations: paid or editorial activity does not guarantee or generate AI citations. Every ranking in this document is derived solely from observed citation data.
Measurement limitation — please readThe dataset does not link an individual citation to an individual brand. What we can measure is co-occurrence: how often a source is cited in an answer that also mentions OMODA or JAECOO. Ecosystem baseline is 17.64%. A low figure means the brands rarely appear in answers built on that source — it does not prove the source supports a competitor.
The core ask
We know which types of article AI keeps citing

This is the conversation to have with every publisher and editorial group — not “can we do something together”, but “these are the formats that get cited, what do you have, and can our models be in them?”

1,072addressable citations from buyer guides & “best of” lists — the biggest format
37.8%of addressable warranty & reliability pieces mention O&J — our strongest format
2.7%of 847 addressable label & ZBE pieces mention O&J
Important reading rule — not every cited page can include our brandsOf the 8,236 citations, 36.1% point to pages about a specific competitor model (a Kia Sorento data sheet, a Skoda Kodiaq review), 60.9% to brand-agnostic pages (buyer guides, comparisons, explainers, category pages) and 3.0% to pages about OMODA or JAECOO. A competitor model page will never mention our brands, so a zero there is not an opportunity — it is structurally unreachable. Those rows are marked competitor model page throughout. The addressable signal below is measured only on brand-agnostic pages.

1 · Label and eligibility content is the biggest single theme

Label / ZBE explainers account for 1167 addressable citations across ECO, CERO, hybrid and PHEV themes, with brand presence of 0.8%. These are the pages AI leans on when someone asks “which SUVs get the ECO label” or “what can enter a low-emission zone”.

Two routes, and they are different jobs: the institutional pages (dgt.es, race.es) are about the accuracy of our model data in reference content; the specialist pieces (movilidadelectrica.com, autopista.es, noticias.coches.com) are about being named as an example model.

2 · Buyer guides on 7-seater and hybrid

7-seater guides: 137 addressable citations at 1.5%. Hybrid guides: 147 at 2.7%. Both are pure editorial inclusion asks, and both sit on reachable platforms — autohero.com, autobild.es, quecochemecompro.com.

Contrast with the same format on other themes: value-for-money guides run at 22.8% and alternatives at 24.3%. The format works for us; the subject matter is where we drop out.

What the two lists say togetherBrand presence is strong wherever the subject is the brand itself — emerging brands, alternatives to mainstream, value for money, warranty. It collapses wherever the subject is a product requirement — which SUV gets the ECO label, which hybrid to buy, which 7-seater fits a family. The reinforcement priority is therefore thematic before it is commercial: get into label/eligibility content and into hybrid and 7-seater buyer guides.

Reading this tablePRISA combines high commercial priority with the strongest detected editorial presence (motor.elpais.com, 67 citations, and notably 44.7% co-occurrence on addressable pages — among the highest of any significant publisher). Vocento and Unidad Editorial are high HAVAS priorities but show only 3 detected citations each today. Two Vocento/Henneo domains from the reference list (mejorcoche.abc.es, heraldo.es) do not appear in this dataset at all; 20minutos.es (Henneo) does, with 11.
3F · Linking opportunities
1

Link editorial and paid-content pieces to the most relevant official OMODA/JAECOO destination, not automatically to the homepage — OMODA 5 content to the OMODA 5 page, JAECOO 7 / 7 PHEV / SHS content to the corresponding model or version page, hybrid / SHS content to the relevant technology or model page, and JAECOO 8 / 7-seater content to the relevant model page.

2

Prioritise contextual links placed inside the body of editorial content, rather than isolated generic brand links.

3

Use natural, descriptive context around each link — model, technology, vehicle category, relevant attribute. Avoid artificial exact-match anchor strategies.

4

Review existing HAVAS paid and editorial content on priority publishers: does it contain a crawlable link, where does it point, is the destination still live, is it the most specific and relevant destination, is model naming correct, and is the article still accurate and current?

5

Where publishers allow updates, review older OMODA/JAECOO content for broken or redirected links, outdated prices, outdated specifications, obsolete model or version naming, and generic homepage links that could point to a specific model page.

6

Prioritise durable editorial and model coverage where possible, rather than relying exclusively on temporary promotional campaign pieces.

Where the brands are strong

Brand presence concentrates in the challenger / emerging brand conversation: 79.8% co-occurrence in Emerging car brands and 27.0% in Alternatives to mainstream.

It falls away in the product and label clusters: ECO-label 1.8%, CERO-label 2.2%, 7-seater 2.4%, Hybrid 4.8%. Those four are where the addressable upside sits.

Actions
Key takeaways

Five recommendations for the OMODA & JAECOO and HAVAS teams.

1
AI answers rely strongly on third-party automotive sources

Automotive specialist media, comparison platforms and marketplaces account for the large majority of citations in both ChatGPT and Gemini. Third-party environments — not brand properties — are where AI answers are assembled.

2
A concentrated group of publishers carries a significant share of citations

The top 20 sources account for roughly half of all citations. OMODA & JAECOO can prioritise a specific, manageable list of external sources instead of dispersing effort across hundreds of domains.

3
The immediate GEO opportunity is to strengthen presence within influential external sources

Prioritise by page type and theme, not only by publisher. Label and eligibility content (ECO, CERO, hybrid) carries 1,117 addressable citations with almost no brand presence; hybrid and 7-seater buyer guides another 284 at under 3%. Those are the briefs with the most upside.

4
Point contextual links to specific model and technology pages

On the most cited publishers, contextual links should point to the most relevant OMODA or JAECOO model / technology page rather than generic brand destinations, with natural descriptive context around each link.

5
Priority sources will be analysed in greater depth in the next GEO Diagnosis phase

Deeper publisher analysis — current OMODA/JAECOO coverage, models mentioned, editorial formats, existing outbound links — plus owned-content optimisation will be addressed separately at that stage.

What these recommendations are notNone of the above claims that buying media will improve AI visibility. The evidence supports one thing: these publishers are the sources AI answers are currently built on, which makes the accuracy, completeness and linkability of OMODA & JAECOO information within them worth managing. Impact must be verified by re-measurement, not assumed.

Data validation, fields used and exclusions
DimensionDataset fieldStatus
PromptFinal promptAvailable · 1,800
ClusterStrategic categoryAvailable · 9
AI modelAI ModelAvailable · 2
ResponseQuery AnswerAvailable · 1,800 non-empty
Mentioned brandsBrand NameAvailable · 1,780 populated

Exclusions: 233 responses carried no grounding URL · 3 malformed URL strings · 5 non-attributable Gemini grounding-redirect citations (vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com). Valid citations retained: 8,236.

Normalisation: host names lower-cased, prefixes www./m./amp./mobile. stripped. Genuinely distinct subdomains representing different publishers or platforms were not merged (es.motor1.com, noticias.coches.com, motor.elpais.com, prensa.toyota.es kept separate). 4,138 unique URLs preserved behind 782 canonical domains.

Scope: 900 non-brand prompts / 1,800 non-brand responses (9 clusters × 100 prompts, one row per Prompt ID + AI Model; 900 ChatGPT GPT-5.2, 900 Gemini 3 Flash). The branded / high-intent layer (3 categories, 300 prompts, 600 responses) is excluded because the workbook carries only its summary, with no response-level grounding URLs. Framework total remains 12 categories · 1,200 prompts · 2,400 responses.

Interpretation limits

A citation demonstrates only that a source appeared in the grounding of an observed response. It does not demonstrate that the source was used to train the model, that the model prefers it generally, or that its presence caused a brand mention. Brand-to-source relationships are reported as co-occurrence; no causal claim is made anywhere in this document. Media activity flags are HAVAS-supplied input, not dataset evidence, and media investment is not claimed to produce AI citations.
